issues: Caption hedge is wrong. It says the 9 November 2025 date 'may be the scan or upload date rather than the date the photograph was taken'. The Commons page's EXIF block reads Camera manufacturer 'OnePlus', Camera model 'OnePlus Open' (a phone released in 2023), 'Date and time of data generation 16:14, 9 November 2025'. The file history shows the upload at '21:36, 27 November 2025' by Kspiers ('Uploaded own work with UploadWizard'). So the photo is a born-digital phone picture, not a scan, and 9 November 2025 is the camera timestamp, not the upload date.

Identity rests only on the uploader's description. Commons description 'Cypherpunk Eric Hughes wearing a black bandana and a nametag with the Luther Blissett pseudonym' (--check FOUND). The face is covered, so the photo cannot confirm who it is. The file is used on en.wikipedia 'Eric Hughes (cypherpunk)', fr/pl Wikipedia and Wikidata Q5386764, but those uses rest on the same uploader claim. The caption should attribute the identification.

Overstatement: the caption calls Syverson 'inventor of onion routing' (copied from the Wikidata description on the Commons page). He was one of three co-inventors. The Tor Project history page says: 'in 1995, David Goldschlag, Michael G. Reed, and Paul Syverson at the U.S. Naval Research Lab (NRL) asked themselves if there was a way to create internet connections that don't reveal who is talking to whom' (--check FOUND). The same page credits the three of them with 'the first research designs and prototypes of onion routing'. The Tor PrivChat page likewise calls him 'one of the authors of the first onion routing paper'.

issues: The licence could not be confirmed as CC BY 3.0. The Commons page carries a CC BY 3.0 tag added by the uploader (Tikmok, 2018), but there is no licence review and no statement of where the licence comes from. The source it cites, svn.torproject.org/svn/projects/design-paper/tor-design.pdf, carries no licence or copyright notice anywhere in its text. The USENIX Security 2004 proceedings copy (usenix.org/legacy/event/sec04/tech/full_papers/dingledine/dingledine.pdf) says: 'Rights to individual papers remain with the author or the author's employer. Permission is granted for noncommercial reproduction of the work for educational or research purposes.' (--check FOUND). That is a noncommercial permission, not CC BY.

A plausible free-licence basis exists, but it is not CC BY. The figure's xfig source, doc/design-paper/interaction.fig, was shipped in the Tor source tree (checked at tag tor-0.1.0.10 on the GitHub mirror). tor-design.tex includes it as \epsfig{figure=interaction}, labelled fig:interaction. The LICENSE file at the same tag says 'Tor is distributed under this license: Copyright (c) 2001-2004, Roger Dingledine; Copyright (c) 2004-2005, Roger Dingledine, Nick Mathewson', followed by 3-clause BSD terms. Syverson's share, as an NRL employee, may be US public domain. So the diagram is probably reusable under Tor's BSD licence, but the record's 'CC BY 3.0' and its credit line are not supported by any source.

Checked OK: content. The paper's caption reads 'Figure 1: Alice builds a two-hop circuit and begins fetching a web page.' (--check FOUND), which matches the record's caption and alt text. The local file opens (960x513 RGB JPEG) and shows Alice, OR 1, OR 2 and the website, with the original 'TLS-encryped' typo. The Commons date '2 August 2004' is not a publication date: the symposium ran 9–13 August 2004 in San Diego. The caption says only '2004', which is fine.

fieldFixes.license: Tagged CC BY 3.0 on Wikimedia Commons (uploader's assertion, no licence review; not supported by the cited source). The figure's source file was distributed in the Tor source tree under Tor's 3-clause BSD licence.
fieldFixes.rightsEvidence: Commons API extmetadata: LicenseShortName "CC BY 3.0"; Artist "Roger Dingledine, Nick Mathewson, Paul Syverson"; Credit "https://svn.torproject.org/svn/projects/design-paper/tor-design.pdf". The Commons page has no licence review. The cited PDF carries no licence. The USENIX Security 2004 printing reserves rights to the authors and grants only noncommercial reproduction. The figure source doc/design-paper/interaction.fig is in the Tor repository (e.g. tag tor-0.1.0.10), whose LICENSE grants 3-clause BSD terms from copyright holders Dingledine and Mathewson. Use only if editors accept the BSD basis, with the credit changed to match; otherwise drop.
